title: Stri: Gandhari's curse
hook: the Pandavas walk toward the mother whose sons they killed, and she has the power to burn them
carry: that's all the burning there is

segments.voice: Yesterday in Stri, the blind king crushed an iron Bhima, and only then embraced the living one. Your line was only an image of iron. Did your anger find somewhere to go first? Today, the victors have to face a mother. Day eight hundred fifty-seven.

The winners of the war have a visit to make, and nobody wants to make it. The five Pandava brothers, with Krishna beside them, have to go and stand in front of Gandhari. She is the queen whose sons fell to them on that field. She has kept her eyes bound with a cloth for her whole married life, the story says, and her years of discipline have given her a power the brothers fear. Her anger could burn. Before they arrive, the sage Vyasa comes to her first. Today, what a grieving mother says to the men who won, and what one glance does.
screen: `THE WINNERS MUST VISIT.` → `A MOTHER WITH BOUND EYES.` → `VYASA COMES FIRST.`

segments.voice: Vyasa reminds Gandhari of something she said herself. All through the war, when Duryodhana came to ask for her blessing, she gave him the same answer: where dharma is, there victory is. She didn't bless him with victory. Now, Vyasa says, the words came true. Don't let anger undo them. So she holds the curse back, but she still has a question, and she puts it to Bhima. Why did you strike my son below the navel, against the rules of the mace fight? Bhima doesn't pretend. He says, in Ganguli's telling, that he was afraid, that Duryodhana could not be beaten fairly, and he reminds her what her son did to Draupadi in the hall. Then she asks the harder thing: did you really drink Duhshasana's blood? Bhima answers that it never passed his lips. Then Gandhari asks for the king. Yudhishthira comes forward, trembling, hands joined, and says it plainly: I killed your sons. Curse me. Gandhari says nothing. But through a small gap in the cloth over her eyes, her gaze falls on the tips of his toes, and his nails, which were fine before, turn dark and damaged. Arjuna, watching, steps behind Krishna. And then her anger passes. She comforts them the way a mother would and sends them to their own mother, Kunti. One look through a sliver of cloth, and that's all the burning there is. The book is named for women, and here a woman holds the power to burn the winners, and mostly chooses not to use it.
screen: `WHERE DHARMA IS, THERE IS VICTORY` · `BHIMA ANSWERS HONESTLY` · `"CURSE ME"` · then, large: `ONE GLANCE AT HIS TOES`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your eyes close, the way Gandhari's were closed. Bring to mind a moment when you had every right to be angry, and you could have said the thing that would have burned. Breathe in, and feel how much heat was there. Breathe out, and notice the space between the heat and the words. You don't have to decide anything about it. Just let the breath sit in that gap. If you pray, you can bring that moment into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Stri. Woman, and the name of the Mahabharata book where the women of both sides finally speak. Today it's Gandhari, holding back a curse she could have spoken.

Your line: that's all the burning there is. Today, when something sharp rises in you, let one breath go by before it leaves your mouth. Tomorrow, Gandhari is given eyes to see the whole field. Day eight hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Storytellers, dance-dramas and modern retellings often return to Gandhari's meeting with the Pandavas, and some readers single out her answer to Duryodhana, where dharma is, there is victory, as the heart of her character.

match.prompt: Gandhari meets the Pandavas — tap the pairs.
pairs: reminds her of her own words

myth: Gandhari blessed Duryodhana to win the war
she told him, where dharma is, there victory is.
a glance through her blindfold marked Yudhishthira's toenails
her gaze fell on the tips of his toes through a gap in the cloth, and the nails turned dark.

her anger passed, and she sent them on to Kunti.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. the mother of every son you killed is waiting, and her anger can burn. what do you do?
options: send Krishna in to speak for you.
stand before her and say, curse me.
wait until her grief has cooled.
fork.reveal: he comes forward, trembling, hands joined, admits he killed her sons and asks her to curse him. she doesn't.

original.note: dharma: in Gandhari's answer to her son, where dharma is, there victory is.

trapdoor: what you thought: Gandhari's curse means she cursed the Pandavas.
what it means: when they come to her, she holds the curse back, and only one glance escapes.
what a scholar hears: Vyasa disarms her with her own words, where dharma is, there victory is, and the book shows her restraint as clearly as her power.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Stri Parva, Vyasa's counsel to Gandhari, her questions to Bhima, and her meeting with Yudhishthira

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli's Stri Parva: Vyasa reminding Gandhari of her repeated answer to Duryodhana ('where dharma is, there victory is'), given here as a paraphrase in quotation-style screen text, not Ganguli's wording.

Confirm Bhima's reply about the blow below the navel and about Duhshasana's blood not passing his lips; confirm Yudhishthira's 'curse me' and the toenail detail (the nails' color is paraphrased as 'dark and damaged').
Confirm Arjuna hiding behind Krishna (Vasudeva) and that Gandhari then sends them to Kunti.
Days 855–856 were not on disk while writing; the review speaks of Stri generally. If those days already cover this meeting, choose another angle.
'Kept her eyes bound for her whole married life' is attributed to the story; confirm the framing is acceptable.
